Lines.Text: BOOM. BOOM. BOOM—!
A heartbeat of bass shook the steel floor backstage.
Behind the dazzling main stage,
P and the five girls waited in the dark.
(calling urgently into a radio) Next act coming up! V.E.L.O., stand by!
The air was hot with the rush of the live broadcast.
In that breathless tension, Ria's fingertips began to tremble.
(taking Ria's shaking hand, whispering) Don't be nervous, Ria. We nailed this with our eyes closed in that pitch-black basement. Remember?
Huff... huff...
(staring coldly ahead) Remember. We don't get another chance.
Anyone messes up on that stage, I'll kill you myself.
(bouncing lightly on the spot) Okay! Those cameras won't know what hit them!
Just like we practiced. Go out there and make damn sure the world remembers who you are.
WHIRRR—
At last, the gate to the stage opened. The girls stepped into the brilliant light.
The heat of hundreds of spectators. Dozens of cameras.
Beneath their feet, the unfamiliar feel of a first-class stage.
As they took their positions, an intro beat powerful enough to burst a heart tore through the studio speakers.
The music began. Their eyes changed.
They devoured the stage like starving predators.
Mina's flawless turns. Seoyun's explosive energy. Ferocious rap pouring from the normally quiet Hana.
Jiwoo's seamless footwork and Ria's piercing vocals.
Honed through agony in that moldy basement,
their performance stole the breath of an audience that had barely cared about this unknown rookie group.
Watching from the wing, P felt heat gather behind his bloodshot eyes.
The song was racing toward its soaring climax.
Ria drew a deep breath. Seoyun moved to burst into center stage.
POP—!!
With a harsh, ear-splitting crack, every light onstage went out.
At the same instant, the thunderous backing track cut off. Completely. Horribly.
Pitch black. Sudden silence.
Bewildered murmurs broke out across the audience.
But on that blacked-out stage, with the lights and music dead...
Where the girls should have frozen in confusion, an uncannily solid, precise rhythm began to sound.
Thud, thud—! Boom—!
Sneakers striking the floor. Fabric slicing through the air.
They had fallen countless times perfecting that choreography in the basement's absolute dark.
Now, without music or light, their movements continued without losing a single second.
Into the silence, Ria forced out the climactic high note with her bare voice, as though tearing blood from her throat.
Seoyun and Mina cut through the dark in time with her desperate singing.
Anything to keep this performance alive. Even one second more.
But this set, crowded with elaborate stage equipment and tangled cables, was nothing like their empty basement.
CRASH—!
Agh!
Crossing to her next position in the dark, Jiwoo caught her foot on a piece of stage equipment and hit the floor with a heavy thud.
Her ankle twisted at a sickening angle. A scream tore out of her.
Jiwoo!!
Something in P snapped.
He shoved past the floor crew blocking him and charged toward the control desk.
(screaming, the veins standing out in his neck) Director! Please, turn the lights on! She's hurt!
They don't have to dance! You don't have to play the music! Just turn the lights back on! Please!
This wasn't a technical fault.
P's eyes darted toward the sound desk.
He saw the lead producer fling down his headset, his face contorted with anger.
(bellowing into his radio) Fuck! S-Tier says if we air these bastards, they're turning all their artists' cars around!
The order came from upstairs—cut them now! Drop the screen and get that trash off my stage!
Money had just forced even the rules of live television to a halt.
(shoving P back by the shoulder, irritated) For fuck's sake! What are you waiting for?! Drag them off!
They saw none of P's desperation, none of the girls'.
Only a nuisance disrupting the running order and angering a powerful agency.
Burly stagehands in black swarmed onto the dark stage.
Nobody asked if the groaning Jiwoo was all right.
They seized both her arms and began to haul her away, as if she were a prop or a piece of equipment to be cleared.
(lunging at a stagehand as if she might bite his arm) Let go! She's hurt!
We'll walk off ourselves, so get your filthy hands off her!
Let go of us! We haven't finished! Let go!
God, what a pain. Hold them still and get them out! We've got another act to set up!
The slight girls had no chance against the strength of grown men.
Mina and Seoyun struggled. Hana cried in terror. Ria stared at the stage with empty eyes,
while Jiwoo clutched her ankle in agony.
All five were dragged across the floor like scraps of dirty rubbish.
(rushing in, trying to pull the stagehands away) You fucking bastards! Get your hands off them! I'll take them out myself!
THWACK—!!
A heavy shoe slammed into P's shin, sending him sprawling.
From the floor, he saw the girls who had danced so brilliantly moments before being thrown out of the backstage area like unwanted baggage.
Right, lights up! Next act on in ten seconds!
As if nothing had happened, the lights blazed again and the next group's cheerful music filled the studio.
Three minutes, thirty seconds. A miracle bought with the girls' blood and sweat, and every scrap of pride P had left.
One phone call from money had thrown it all into the trash before they had made it past two minutes.
As far as the world was concerned, those invisible people, those who had crossed the industry's money, had never stood on its stage at all.
